findings_qualitative.value: A collimated molecular jet (~±150 pc, unresolved width) with velocity reversals along its axis, consistent with precession

evidence.quote: we have discovered a high velocity, collimated molecular jet with a projected length of $\pm$150 pc

claims.hypothesis: The high-velocity CO 3-2 gas is a precessing molecular jet
claims.experiment: PV diagrams along and across the jet compared with a simple precession model and a bicone alternative
claims.result: Velocity reversals of about ±150 km/s; narrow transverse PV shapes disfavour a cone
claims.finding: A precessing jet with v_out 240-850 km/s and P 0.3-1.1 Myr is favoured

evidence.quote: A simple model of a molecular jet precessing around an axis close to the plane of the sky can reproduce the observations.

claims.hypothesis: The jet signals SMBH growth or quenching
claims.experiment: Energetics for light and massive jet cases
claims.result: Jet mass 2e6-2e7 Msun depending on the conversion factor
claims.finding: Cannot decide between growth and quenching

evidence.quote: it is difficult to draw conclusions on whether the jet is quenching the nuclear activity or, instead, is enabling it.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Orbiting SMBH, jet shocks and a projected bicone were considered and judged less likely than a precessing jet

evidence.quote: this seems unlikely compared to the relatively simple scenario of one single precessing jet.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution is insufficient for proper model fits; the jet mass is uncertain because of the CO-to-H2 conversion factor

evidence.quote: We require higher spatial resolution to carry out proper model fits to the jet properties.

referee_caveats_inferred: The jet model is illustrative and has no formal fit or uncertainties
The 3-2 to 1-0 conversion and the CO-to-H2 factor strongly affect the masses and rates
